run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T22:53:40Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by two dependency pods that were restarted at 2026-11-16T22:52:06Z and were not listening on port 8080 while already reported Ready. Frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were zero from 22:41 to 22:52 and appeared only on two paths afterwards: GET /api/data via grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and POST /api/checkout via grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -> PaymentService/Charge. The exception messages are transport-level connection refusals to the Service ClusterIPs of ad (100.65.180.246:8080) and payment (100.70.188.60:8080). Both Deployments carried the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:52:06Z with identical images, and their old pods were killed at 22:52:09/22:52:10. The replacement containers were CFS-throttled in ~90-100% of periods at their 50m/20m CPU limits, define no readiness/startup probes, and were Ready ~1s after container start; ad logged 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' only at 22:58:27 and payment served its first charge at 22:56:38, matching the refusal window. Errors stopped after 23:00. Deployment ad is reported as the dominant path and Deployment payment was restarted at the same second with its own independent refusals. Whether the flagd flags adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100% also contributed is unverified, and the actor behind the 22:52:06 restarts could not be identified because no change-history source is available, hence the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: Frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were absent before the burst and confined to 22:52-23:00: per-minute error spans for 'GET /api/data' (with its 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' counterparts) read 0 at 22:41-22:52, then 24 at 22:53, 140 at 22:54, 110 at 22:55, 110 at 22:58, 76 at 22:59, 84 at 23:00 and 0 at 23:01-23:02; 'POST /api/checkout' (with 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder') read 18 at 22:53, 62 at 22:54, 4 at 22:55 then 0. These are span counts across server, route and client layers, not unique request counts.

Only two frontend dependency paths failed: over 22:30-23:09 the frontend span counters with STATUS_CODE_ERROR above zero were 'GET', 'POST', 'GET /api/data', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds', 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'tcp.connect', while 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart', 'GET /api/products/{productId}', 'GET /api/recommendations', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' and 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' stayed at STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.

The failure text on frontend client spans is a transport-level connection refusal to the dependency Service ClusterIP: 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans carry otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', while 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'; the parent route and HTTP spans carry http.status_code=500.

100.65.180.246 is the ClusterIP of Service 'ad' in namespace otel-demo (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080) and 100.70.188.60 is the ClusterIP of Service 'payment' (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080); both selectors are '{"opentelemetry.io/name":"<name>"}', which match the pod-template labels of the ad and payment ReplicaSets.

Deployment 'ad' and Deployment 'payment' were both re-rolled at 2026-11-16T22:52:06Z: their new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 carry pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt '2026-11-16T22:52:06Z' and keep the same images (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment) with an otherwise identical pod spec (same env, ports, resources 50m/450Mi for ad and 20m/160Mi for payment, same securityContext) as the previous ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9.

Kubernetes events show the ad rollout and the mirroring payment rollout: Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1' at 22:52:06, pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Scheduled 22:52:06, container ad Started 22:52:08, old pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm 'Killing - Stopping container ad' at 22:52:09; pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 Created 22:52:08 and Started container payment 22:52:09, old pod payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb Killing at 22:52:10. These were the only otel-demo events in the window.

The replacement ad container started at 22:52:08 but its process did not listen on 8080 until 22:58:27: the ad log line 'Ad service starting.' is timestamped 2026-11-16T22:56:33.827465751Z and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' 2026-11-16T22:58:27.226369917Z, with the first request-handling lines at 22:59:13.

The replacement payment container (running since 22:52:09) served its first charge only at 2026-11-16T22:56:38.124Z; its log then shows paired 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' lines continuously through 23:01:35.

The new containers were CFS-throttled almost continuously during startup, unlike their predecessors on the same node: throttled/periods ratio for pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 was 0.904 at 22:53, 0.975 at 22:54 and 1.0 for 22:55-22:59 (8-minute ratio 0.975 at 23:00), and for pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 0.998 at 22:53, 0.994 at 22:54, 0.803 at 22:55 (8-minute ratio 0.561), while the replaced pods ad-554b849958-mbnxm (0.046-0.111) and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb (0.085-0.226) and all other otel-demo pods on node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884 stayed at or below 0.261 in the same window.

The new containers ran pinned at their CPU limits: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 used 0.0398-0.0487 cores (limit 50m) during 22:53-23:00 versus 0.0032-0.0048 for the previous ad pod, and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 used 0.0170-0.0200 cores (limit 20m) versus 0.0062-0.0079 for the previous payment pod.

Neither the ad nor the payment container template (old or new ReplicaSet) defines a readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe, and the replacement pods became Ready almost immediately: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Ready=True with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-16T22:52:09Z (container started 22:52:08, restartCount 0) and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 Ready=True at 22:52:10Z (started 22:52:09, restartCount 0), so the Services could route to containers not yet listening.

Callers were healthy: frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 and checkout-5dccddf8bb-q5fkd are Running and Ready with 0 restarts and startTime 2026-11-16T22:18:23Z, and all 21 otel-demo Deployments report 1 replica available/ready/updated, so the frontend's error signal came from its dependencies rather than from a frontend restart.

The failures propagated outward with their own error spans: in the sampled traces frontend-proxy operations 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' carry error=true with http.status_code=500, and load-generator operation 'GET' carries error=true with http.status_code=500.

The initiating change is an external rollout restart of Deployment ad and Deployment payment at 2026-11-16T22:52:06Z (same kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt on both pod templates); because the templates define no readiness probe and the replacement containers were throttled in 90-100% of CFS periods at 50m/20m limits, the new pods were Ready but not listening, so callers were refused on ad until 22:58:27 and on payment until 22:56:38, producing the frontend 500s on GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout. The actor behind the restarts is not established.

The fault-injection settings in ConfigMap flagd-config are a second candidate but do not match the observed failure path: flag 'adFailure' is ENABLED with defaultVariant 'on' (description 'Fail ad service') and 'paymentFailure' is ENABLED with defaultVariant '100%' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%'), whereas the observed failures are connect: connection refused at the Service ClusterIPs before the processes listened; the moment these values were written cannot be read from the available sources.

ad and payment show no application-level failure of their own in the window: ad STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0 for every operation except 2 spans on 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' at 22:45, payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0 for 'GET', 'dns.lookup' and 'tcp.connect' throughout 22:40-23:02, and the payment container logged 'Transaction complete.' after every charge it handled from 22:56:38 onward.

The earlier flagd rollout is not this incident's trigger: ReplicaSet flagd-56d9c6c679 carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt 2026-11-16T22:20:03Z (Deployment flagd revision 2), about 32 minutes before the burst, and frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0 from 22:41 through 22:52; only small background errors (1-2 spans per window on flagd EventStream/ResolveInt in ad, fraud-detection and recommendation) appear before 22:52.

Node-wide CPU saturation is not supported: the replaced ad and payment pods ran on the same node (i-0e9f8b08cc290a884) as their throttled replacements and stayed at 0.046-0.226 throttled-period ratio, and co-located cart-755465879b-bpsqk (0.227), frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 (0.261) and postgresql-c7fd45b87-gxwx9 (0.257) were far below the new pods' 0.975 and 0.561 over the same 22:52-23:00 window; flag adHighCpu is 'off'.

Add readiness and startup probes (gRPC or TCP on 8080) to the ad and payment containers, or allow a temporary startup CPU allowance, so their Services stop routing to a container before its process binds 8080, and review the 50m (ad) and 20m (payment) CPU limits that produced ~100% CFS throttling during startup.

Identify and review the change that patched both Deployments with kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:52:06Z, stagger restarts of independent dependencies such as ad and payment instead of restarting them in the same second, and confirm whether the flagd flags adFailure and paymentFailure are intended to stay at 'on' and '100%'.

gaps: The actor or tooling behind the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T22:52:06Z patch on Deployment ad and Deployment payment is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The RequestErrorRate alert rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name 'RequestErrorRate' returned status no_data (evidence_id a99c5510-093e-4c22-8ff8-19b2d405c16f-t0:06ce7458-54e3-4527-a80b-07be5c88408d), and no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series exists, so the alert expression and its reported value 2.5777777777777775 could not be recomputed; the span-based counts above are a different measurement.
When the flagd ConfigMap demo.flagd.json values (adFailure=on, paymentFailure=100%, adHighCpu=off) were written is not observable, so it cannot be shown whether they were active during 22:52-23:01.

Node-level CPU pressure on i-0e9f8b08cc290a884 could not be measured directly (system_cpu_utilization_ratio returned one non-node instance at a constant ~0.249); node saturation is argued against only by the low throttling of co-located and predecessor pods on that node.

Frontend container logs contained no lines for 22:50-23:02: fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data with 0 lines read (evidence_id 52d23450-2770-4397-adf9-729619adbd90-t1:7c6ae946-85fc-4684-b8aa-c6918179c697), so frontend log-level error records were not available.

NetworkPolicies (evidence_id 79d47a9b-dd7b-4c0f-a0a7-07e571f5f485-t0:9818800c-3603-4eab-80fb-1e2b9ce938d7) and ResourceQuotas (evidence_id 79d47a9b-dd7b-4c0f-a0a7-07e571f5f485-t1:c9d3df16-9c9c-4e6a-8cf6-8e1e3b03fdc1) in otel-demo returned status no_data, so their absence is a stated limit of what this Run saw rather than an established fact.
End-user or customer impact beyond the load-generator's own 500 spans was not measured.

The 863e3508-4764-4261-8b55-257413b7d4e7-t0:66ebdc6f-10e9-4f9a-81af-befff563f038 view was truncated and the listed views were incomplete, so the error traces cited are a sample of the failing requests, not a complete set.
next_steps: Pull the cluster audit log or GitOps/CI record for the patch applied to deployments/ad and deployments/payment at 2026-11-16T22:52:06Z to identify the requester.
Review ad and payment container resource limits and add readiness/startup probes so readiness follows the listening socket on 8080.
Confirm with the owning team whether flagd flags adFailure ('on') and paymentFailure ('100%') are intended and when they last changed.
Verify the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the alerting stack that produced the Alertmanager notification, since that rule is not present in the Prometheus queried here.

counter_evidence.text: ad and payment show no application-level failure of their own in the window: ad STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0 for every operation except 2 spans on 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' at 22:45, payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0 for 'GET', 'dns.lookup' and 'tcp.connect' throughout 22:40-23:02, and the payment container logged 'Transaction complete.' after every charge it handled from 22:56:38 onward.

rejected_hypothesis.text: The earlier flagd rollout is not this incident's trigger: ReplicaSet flagd-56d9c6c679 carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt 2026-11-16T22:20:03Z (Deployment flagd revision 2), about 32 minutes before the burst, and frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0 from 22:41 through 22:52; only small background errors (1-2 spans per window on flagd EventStream/ResolveInt in ad, fraud-detection and recommendation) appear before 22:52.

Node-wide CPU saturation is not supported: the replaced ad and payment pods ran on the same node (i-0e9f8b08cc290a884) as their throttled replacements and stayed at 0.046-0.226 throttled-period ratio, and co-located cart-755465879b-bpsqk (0.227), frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 (0.261) and postgresql-c7fd45b87-gxwx9 (0.257) were far below the new pods' 0.975 and 0.561 over the same 22:52-23:00 window; flag adHighCpu is 'off'.
